acceptance_evidence.criterion: Exact stable worker and controller identity, private transport, and runtime identity are verified.
Restricted Local Service worker, minimal manifest-bound bundle, and worker-owned pinned runtime are deployed.
Three fixed deterministic tranches and one exact-dedup pilot replay byte-identically.
Worker/controller restart, interrupted-job recovery, invalid/corrupt/expired/unauthorized packet rejection, disk admission, hash validation, and cleanup pass.
No public Funnel, arbitrary execution, credentials in evidence, canonical writes, or protected decisions are introduced.

negative_findings_preserved: The initial Serve attempt stalled because tailnet HTTPS certificates were disabled; HTTPS was enabled through the authenticated admin console before qualification.
The first implementation depended on user-profile Python and was not deployed; it was replaced by a Sigstore-verified CPython embeddable runtime.
The first corrected worker lacked stale lease/scratch startup recovery; the gap was fixed and empirically exercised before qualification.
The first sealing retry reused a fixed nonce with a fresh timestamp and was correctly rejected; qualification run identity now prevents that conflict.
completion_claim: BAT-563 qualification is complete at the deterministic qualified-candidate level. This does not establish unified sustained operation or general remote execution authority.
protected_nonclaims: No unified-plane fully operational or seven-day sustained-operation claim.
No canonical, PIT, model-promotion, forecast, publication, production, protected-performance, A&M-lift, BAS, Aggie Excess, or other scientific-result claim.
